dev-w-identity-youth-crisis.summary: In this book Erikson develops the concept of "identity crisis." It is a starting point for understanding young people's self-exploration.

dev-w-nature-of-love.summary: Rhesus monkeys preferred a soft cloth "mother" to a wire "mother" that provided milk, showing that attachment is not only about food.
dev-w-nature-of-love.enRec.note: Journal article, easy to find online

dev-w-patterns-attachment.summary: Ainsworth and her colleagues report the Strange Situation experiments and propose three attachment patterns: secure, avoidant and ambivalent.
dev-w-patterns-attachment.enRec.note: First edition; later reprinted by Psychology Press

dev-w-philosophy-moral-development.summary: The first volume of Essays on Moral Development. In it Kohlberg systematically presents the three levels and six stages of moral development and the idea of justice.

dev-w-baumrind-1966.summary: Baumrind distinguishes authoritative, authoritarian and permissive parenting. It is the starting point of research on parenting styles.

dev-w-successful-aging.summary: Includes the "selection, optimization and compensation" model proposed by Baltes and his wife, which explains how people maintain function despite decline.

dev-w-beliefs-about-beliefs.summary: Introduces the false-belief task: whether children can predict that another person will act on a mistaken belief.

dev-w-object-permanence-5-month.summary: Baillargeon and colleagues used experiments with "possible and impossible events" to show that five-month-old infants appear to "know" that a hidden object still exists.

dev-w-what-babies-know.summary: Spelke summarizes thirty years of infant experiments and argues that humans are born with a core knowledge of objects, number and space.

dev-w-role-of-tutoring.summary: Bruner and colleagues propose "scaffolding": adults give appropriate support where a child cannot yet manage, and withdraw it as the child improves.

soc-w-principles-topological-psychology.summary: Lewin uses the "life space" to describe the relationship between people and their environment, and proposes that behavior is a function of person and environment.

soc-w-field-theory-social-science.summary: A collection of papers published after Lewin's death, including articles on group dynamics, leadership climate and action research.

soc-w-work-and-motivation.summary: Vroom proposes expectancy theory: motivation depends on a person's judgment about whether effort will lead to outcomes and whether those outcomes are valuable.

soc-w-asch-group-pressure.summary: Asch's original report of the line-judgment experiments, included in the collection Groups, Leadership and Men.
soc-w-asch-group-pressure.enRec.note: A chapter in a collection; a standalone edition is hard to find

soc-w-unresponsive-bystander.summary: Through a series of experiments, Latané and Darley show that the more bystanders there are, the less likely each person is to step in and help.

soc-w-authoritarian-personality.summary: Exiled scholars working with American psychologists studied the personality roots of prejudice and authoritarian tendencies. Its methods and conclusions are much debated.
soc-w-authoritarian-personality.enRec.note: First edition; later reprinted by Norton

soc-w-whistling-vivaldi.summary: Steele tells the story of how stereotype threat was discovered and how it affects performance on tests and at work.

soc-w-blindspot.summary: Two designers of the Implicit Association Test discuss research on implicit bias and openly acknowledge the test's limitations.

soc-w-theory-cognitive-dissonance.summary: Festinger proposes that when a person's beliefs and behavior contradict each other, they feel discomfort and look for ways to reduce it.
soc-w-theory-cognitive-dissonance.enRec.note: Stanford University Press paperback, the standard version

soc-w-strangers-to-ourselves.summary: Wilson explains how people often infer their own attitudes by observing their own behavior, and how much less they understand their own minds than they assume.

soc-w-person-and-situation.summary: Ross and Nisbett explain that people consistently underestimate the power of situations and overestimate personal character, and discuss the consequences.

soc-w-face-and-favor.summary: Proposes Hwang Kwang-Kuo's model of renqing and face as a resource-exchange model. It is a representative theory of indigenous Chinese psychology.

soc-w-social-categorization-1971.summary: The minimal group experiments: people favor their own group even when the groups are assigned at random.

soc-w-automaticity-social-behavior.summary: Proposes experiments in which priming the stereotype of the elderly made people walk more slowly. Many priming effects of this kind later failed to replicate.

soc-w-social-cognition-fiske-taylor.summary: The first textbook in the field of social cognition. It describes people as "cognitive misers" and covers schemas, attribution and impression formation.
soc-w-social-cognition-fiske-taylor.enRec.note: First edition; later updated editions exist

soc-w-pygmalion-classroom.summary: Reports experiments showing that teacher expectations affect student performance. Its conclusions were later criticized on methodological grounds.

soc-w-foolproof.summary: Describes how misinformation spreads and introduces "psychological inoculation": showing people manipulation techniques in advance, much as a vaccine works.

hum-w-will-to-meaning.summary: Frankl systematically presents the theory of logotherapy and describes the practice of paradoxical intention.
hum-w-will-to-meaning.enRec.note: Expanded edition with a new chapter

hum-w-positivity.summary: Fredrickson explains how positive emotions broaden attention and build resources, and acknowledges that more positivity is not always better.

hum-w-grit.summary: Duckworth argues that long-term passion and perseverance predict achievement better than talent. The predictive power of this claim has been qualified by later research.

hum-w-client-centered-therapy.summary: In this book Rogers systematically sets out the theory and practice of client-centered therapy.
hum-w-client-centered-therapy.enRec.note: First edition; a reprint by Constable is available in the UK

hum-w-existence-may.summary: A collection of essays that introduced European existential analysis and phenomenological psychiatry to American readers.

hum-w-eft-couples-book.summary: The two founders explain the theory and practice of emotionally focused couple therapy, combining attachment with emotional processes.

dep-w-discovery-unconscious.summary: A general history of depth psychology, from hypnosis and Charcot through Janet to Freud and Jung.
dep-w-discovery-unconscious.enRec.note: First edition; later reprinted by Fontana

dep-w-rewriting-soul.summary: The philosopher Hacking examines the rise of multiple personality and its relation to memory science, and discusses how this diagnosis was "made" in the first place.

dep-w-studies-hysteria.summary: A collection of case studies by Breuer and Freud, the starting point of psychoanalysis. It discusses repression and the "talking cure."
dep-w-studies-hysteria.enRec.note: A newer translation, easier to read

dep-w-ego-and-id.summary: Freud proposes the structural model of the id, ego and superego.

dep-w-what-life-should-mean.summary: Adler's late book for a general readership, discussing inferiority, lifestyle and birth order.
dep-w-what-life-should-mean.enRec.note: First edition; later reprinted by several publishers

dep-w-psychoanalysis-of-children.summary: Klein analyzes children through play and proposes that young children already have a rich inner world of objects.
dep-w-psychoanalysis-of-children.enRec.note: English translation, published almost at the same time as the German edition

dep-w-envy-gratitude.summary: Collects Klein's papers after 1946, including her classic description of the paranoid-schizoid position.
dep-w-envy-gratitude.enRec.note: Volume 3 of her collected works, including "On Some Schizoid Mechanisms"

dep-w-wisdom-of-ego.summary: Based on long-term follow-up, Vaillant arranges defense mechanisms in a hierarchy according to their maturity.

dep-w-interpersonal-theory-psychiatry.summary: Sullivan's lectures, arguing that personality is formed through interaction within important relationships.

dep-w-origins-history-consciousness.summary: Neumann uses myth to describe the process by which consciousness emerges from the unconscious. It is a founding work of the post-Jungian school.
dep-w-origins-history-consciousness.enRec.note: Standard English translation; there is also a Princeton Classics edition

dep-w-sandplay-kalff.summary: Kalff combined Lowenfeld's "World Technique" with Jungian psychology to form sandplay therapy.
dep-w-sandplay-kalff.enRec.note: English translation, published by Sigo Press

dep-w-jung-active-imagination.summary: Chodorow's selection of Jung's writings on active imagination, including "Transcendent Function," with an editor's introduction.
dep-w-jung-active-imagination.enRec.note: A selection of Jung's writings on the subject

dep-w-symbols-transformation.summary: Jung's analysis of a woman's fantasies, which reinterprets libido through myth. It was a trigger for his break with Freud.
dep-w-symbols-transformation.enRec.note: Volume 5 of the Collected Works, translated from the 1952 revised edition

dep-w-experimental-researches.summary: Collects Jung's papers on association experiments from 1904 to 1910, including his 1907 study recording the skin galvanic response with a galvanometer.
dep-w-experimental-researches.enRec.note: Volume 2 of the Collected Works, including papers on word association and the galvanic skin response

dep-w-modern-man-soul.summary: A collection of Jung's popular essays, including "The Stages of Life," which discusses the midlife turning point and the tasks of the second half of life.
dep-w-modern-man-soul.enRec.note: Classic series reprint of the 1933 English translation

dep-w-gifts-differing.summary: Myers's own explanation of type theory and the MBTI. It is primary material for understanding the indicator.

dep-w-bonds-of-love.summary: Benjamin uses "mutual recognition" to describe intimate relationships. It is a representative account of intersubjectivity in relational psychoanalysis.

cli-w-training-clinical-psychology.summary: The report of the 1949 Boulder Conference, which established the model of training clinical psychologists as both scientists and practitioners.

cli-w-dementia-praecox-paraphrenia.summary: Kraepelin distinguished dementia praecox from manic-depressive illness according to the course of illness. The English version is based on his later editions.
cli-w-dementia-praecox-paraphrenia.enRec.note: English version based on the relevant chapters of the eighth edition; later reprinted by Krieger

cli-w-bleuler-dementia-praecox.summary: Bleuler introduced the term "schizophrenia" and treated it as a group of disorders rather than a single form of dementia.

cli-w-on-being-sane.summary: A study in which pseudopatients got admitted to psychiatric hospitals. Its validity and methods were later questioned.

cli-w-reason-emotion-psychotherapy.summary: Ellis sets out rational emotive behavior therapy and the ABC model: distress comes from irrational beliefs about events.

cli-w-toward-theory-schizophrenia.summary: Proposes the "double bind": when a person receives contradictory messages over a long period and cannot respond, psychotic symptoms may appear. The hypothesis was largely abandoned later.

cli-w-families-family-therapy.summary: Minuchin proposes structural family therapy, which looks at family boundaries, alliances and hierarchies and changes symptoms through restructuring.

cli-w-expressed-emotion-families.summary: Summarizes how criticism, hostility and over-involvement from family members predict relapse in schizophrenia.

cli-w-great-psychotherapy-debate.summary: Uses meta-analysis to argue that different therapies are roughly equally effective, and that outcomes depend more on common factors and the therapeutic relationship.

cli-w-vulnerability-schizophrenia.summary: Proposes the stress-vulnerability model: a predisposition formed by genes or early experience becomes illness when enough stress is present.

cli-w-cognitive-behavior-modification.summary: Meichenbaum combines behavioral techniques with changes in self-talk. It marks the integration of cognitive behavioral therapy.

cli-w-behavioral-activation-guide.summary: A therapist's guide to behavioral activation: improving depression by scheduling valued activities.

cli-w-erp-ocd-therapist-guide.summary: A practical manual for exposure and response prevention for obsessive-compulsive disorder, describing the course of treatment session by session.

cli-w-cognitive-approach-panic.summary: Proposes that panic attacks arise from catastrophic interpretations of bodily sensations, and designs treatment on that basis.

cli-w-prolonged-exposure-guide.summary: A therapist's manual for prolonged exposure therapy, describing in concrete terms how imaginal and in vivo exposure are carried out.

cli-w-cpt-manual.summary: A complete manual for cognitive processing therapy, focusing on the beliefs that keep people "stuck" after trauma.

cli-w-getting-past-your-past.summary: A book for general readers by the founder of EMDR, introducing the approach and self-help exercises.

cli-w-mbct-depression.summary: A manual by the founders of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, using an eight-week course to prevent relapse in depression.

cli-w-compassionate-mind.summary: Gilbert draws on evolution and attachment to explain compassion-focused therapy, and offers exercises for cultivating compassion.

cli-w-linehan-bpd.summary: Linehan systematically sets out the theory and techniques of dialectical behavior therapy.

cli-w-posttraumatic-growth-2004.summary: Summarizes the concept and evidence of posttraumatic growth, and cautions that growth and suffering can coexist.

cli-w-hitop-2017.summary: The manifesto paper of the consortium proposing that psychopathology be organized by dimensions and hierarchies rather than diagnostic categories.

cli-w-p-factor-2014.summary: Uses long-term cohort data to suggest that a common "p factor" may underlie the various psychiatric disorders.
